chapter_theme: The six ends (ஆறு அந்தம்): Vedanta, Siddhanta, the end of nada, the end of knowing, the end of yoga and the end of the kalas. Each is defined, and all subside into the one known where knower and knowing vanish in silence and Siva's bliss. Vedanta and Siddhanta are one; the Veda and the Agama are both the Lord's word; and tat tvam asi is read in Saiva terms as the bound soul, the Lord and their union, sayujya.
structure_note: 2370 names the six ends and 2371 praises those who know them. 2372 to 2380 define them in turn: Vedanta and Siddhanta (2372, 2373), nadanta (2374), bodhanta (2375), yoganta (2376) and kalanta with its further kalas (2377 to 2380). 2381 to 2383 gather them into the known and into silence. 2384 to 2391 turn to the Lord who taught them and works through Shakti. 2392 to 2404 argue the unity of Vedanta and Siddhanta, of Veda and Agama, and read tat tvam asi (2387, 2392, 2402). 2399 and 2400 count the ends as five, with Vedanta and Siddhanta as one.

2370.reading: The end of the Veda, the excellent Siddhanta, the end of nada, the good end of knowing, the end of the bliss of the eightfold yoga that is worth reciting, and the end of the primal kalas: these are the six ends.
2370.nuance: The list gives the chapter's six terms: வேதாந்தம், சித்தாந்தம், நாதாந்தம், போதாந்தம், யோகாந்தம், கலாந்தம். Calling Siddhanta an அந்தம் beside Vedanta puts the two on a level, which the chapter goes on to argue.

2371.reading: Those who know the six ends are the most pure; those who know the six ends are free of malam; those who do not know the six ends cannot know the end and the beginning.
2371.nuance: The last line plays on அந்தம்: not knowing the ends, one cannot know 'end and beginning', taken as the Lord who is both.

2372.reading: Vedanta, which has become the self, and Siddhanta, which says it is the self: seeing the soul in unending turiya and joining the honeyed Supreme as Siva-yoga, the malam that does not end is removed and one comes to the rare attainment.
2372.nuance: தானான and தான்என்னும் separate the two only slightly: Vedanta as having become the self, Siddhanta as declaring it. துரியம் is the fourth state beyond waking, dream and sleep, and அணுவன் the soul as anu, both technical. ஆனா மலம் may be 'the malam that does not end of itself'.

2373.reading: Siddhanta is this: the soul ever joined with the Supreme, the restless mind and the five beginning with sound removed by knowing the tattvas, holding in thought that neither pure nor impure follows it, and reaching the Father, the Supreme.
2373.nuance: சத்தம் முதல் ஐந்து are the five subtle elements beginning with sound. சுத்தம் அசுத்தம் may be pure and impure maya, or good and bad deeds; the verse does not say.

2374.reading: Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, the acting Isa, Sadasiva, and beyond them the supreme bindu and nada: when the thirty-six that do not leave cease, the soul alone remains.
2374.nuance: The five deities and bindu and nada are the ascending ranks of the tattvas; ஆறாறு is the thirty-six. அணு is the Siddhanta term for the soul. Placed after 2373, this is taken as the account of nadanta, though the verse does not name it.

2375.reading: Sifting away the adjunct of the thirty-six that the living soul bears, going past the end of nada, when the darkness above is removed it becomes one awareness: that is the knowing reached at the end of nada.
2375.nuance: The closing போதம் suggests this is bodhanta, the end of knowing. உபாதி (limiting adjunct) is a Vedanta term. செற்று (having destroyed, or pressed past) and எள்ளலின் in the last line are unclear.

2376.reading: Passing beyond yama, niyama and the rest that are sought, entering samadhi, Siva spreading through, the soul becoming the Supreme with attachment gone, the union in perfect calm: that is the doctrine of yoganta.
2376.nuance: இயம நியமாதி are the first limbs of eightfold yoga, so the end of yoga is reached by going beyond its steps. உபசாந்தம் is a technical term for complete stillness. படர்சிவன் பாடுற is unclear.

2377.reading: If one marks kalanta in this doctrine: it is bindu, which belongs to the kalas beginning with nivritti and medha that appear as things unfold, withdrawing within, and clearly discerning it.
2377.nuance: நிவிர்த்தாதி names the five kalas from nivritti, a standard Siddhanta set; மேதாதி is less clear and may be a set of kalas of the syllable Om. விள்கை (unfolding) and ஒடுங்கல் (withdrawing) make kalanta the reversal of the kalas back into bindu.

2378.reading: Besides these discerned kalas there are five other kalas, set within light, for those able to examine: given by the gracious one, they are mantra, tantra, clear teaching and knowledge, five in all.
2378.nuance: The count is unclear: mantra, tantra, upadesa and jnana make four, and the fifth may be the gracious one (அளியவன்) himself or something the text has lost. 2379 goes on to define them.

2379.reading: The beginningless kala is the Agama and the Veda; tantra is standing in the way those scriptures lay down; mantra is the beginningless one who is not body; upadesa is the teaching that is knowledge of Siva.
2379.nuance: The verse defines the five of 2378 in Tirumular's own terms: tantra is practice according to scripture, not a separate text. உடல்அல்லா மந்திரம் may mean mantra as the bodiless Lord, or the Lord whose body is mantra, as the Agamas say.

2380.reading: The kala of one's own knowledge that becomes radiant Siva, and conduct, love and the Veda too, end in kalanta; the great one beyond speech, word and feeling, beyond speech and mind, is great Nandi himself.
2380.nuance: வாசாமகோசரம் is taken as the Sanskrit phrase for what speech and mind cannot reach. ஆசார நேய மறையும் may mean conduct, love and Veda all end there, or that conduct and love 'disappear' (மறையும்) in kalanta.

2381.reading: If one reaches the samadhi in which oneself becomes He, kalanta, nadanta and yoganta, and the others, bodhanta and Siddhanta, become knowledge, the known and the knower.
2381.nuance: ஞானம், ஞேயம், ஞாதுரு are the triad of knowing, known and knower. The verse does not say which end becomes which, and Vedanta is not named, perhaps because it is one with Siddhanta.

2382.reading: The six ends all go and subside in that known; the knower too subsides in the known of the six ends; when even the stated mark of knowledge departs, the clear silence becomes Siva's bliss.
2382.nuance: The triad of 2381 collapses in order: the ends into the known, the knower into the known, then knowledge itself. What remains is மோனம், silence, as a state, and it is named as bliss.

2383.reading: The true kalas, six, are held in one five; true kalanta is two with five, seven ends; and in nadanta, the end within one kala, to speak the true kala is one end.
2383.nuance: The verse is a count of kalas and ends whose scheme I can't recover; உண்மைக் கலை (true kala) opens every line. The numbers are given as read, not reconciled.

2384.reading: After Hara came and took hold of the one who has the soul, our glorious divine Nandi gave his feet; think on the king who taught, unfailing, the greatness of Vedanta and Siddhanta.
2384.nuance: ஆவுடையான் is unclear: ஆ (cow) is a Saiva figure for the soul, so 'the one who owns the soul', but it may also echo ஆவுடையார, the lingam's pedestal. கூளி in line 4 gives no fitting sense and may be கூறி (having told).

2385.reading: In the Agama that Hara spoke and gave in grace to fit the thought of those who think on him lies the truth of Vedanta and Siddhanta, which passes through the outer sects, maya and great maya.
2385.nuance: Line 1 says the Lord's teaching is shaped to its hearers. உருவிய can mean 'piercing through' or 'drawn out from', so the truth either goes beyond the outer sects and the two mayas or is drawn out of them.

2386.reading: Vedanta and Siddhanta are a seal without difference; the knowledge of bodhanta, yoganta, the shared known of nadanta and bliss become a rising of glory when one sinks into the silence of the seal of the ancient end.
2386.nuance: முத்திரை here is a seal or mark of identity more than a hand gesture; மூதாந்த முத்திரை, the seal of the ancient end, is unclear. The verse gathers the ends again and ends them in silence, as 2382 does.

2387.reading: In Vedanta, when the seven adjuncts are left, the good 'thou' is what leaves the bond at the end of nada; beyond, with the seven causal adjuncts gone, the true Supreme is the 'that' of bodhanta; and their joining, they say, is 'art'.
2387.nuance: தொம்பதம், தற்பதம் and அசி are the three words of tat tvam asi ('that thou art'). The verse assigns 'thou' to the soul freed at nadanta and 'that' to the Lord at bodhanta. The two sets of seven adjuncts are not identified, and போமசி may be போம் அசி (the joining is asi).

2388.reading: Beyond the seven worlds and further, within the great light said to be there, is an inner light called the ancient Parashakti; and our King stood there as the one who holds her, yet not as her.
2388.nuance: கொண்டவன் அன்றி நின்றான் can mean he stood as the one who holds her, or stood apart from what he holds; Siddhanta's Lord is one with his Shakti yet not reduced to her. Sengalvaraya cites Appar 6-97-1 on what lies beyond the worlds.

2389.reading: The King knows through Shakti and, setting the aim, has the acts done that make the gods know; creating all that is imagined and spreading worship, he is the One who is in all and never ceases.
2389.nuance: The syntax is broken into odd units (கோஉணர்ந் தும், ஓஅனைத் துண்டு), which makes the reading tentative. அனைத்துண்டு may be 'is in all' or 'has consumed all', the latter pointing to dissolution.

2390.reading: They do not think of the One, nor of the soul, nor of the two kinds of deed, nor of the two mayas; yet the One alone, knowing within, stands and feeds them, the formless one who is their support.
2390.nuance: Line 1 names the categories: the Lord, the soul, deeds and maya. Whether it faults the ignorant who ignore them or describes the freed who no longer think of them is open. ஊட்டி (feeding) is taken as making souls experience the fruit of their deeds.

2391.reading: Hara becomes the place of his devotees; setting out first the powers that arise in Siva so that his mighty presence acts, he is ever the steady one of Siva's bliss whom nothing touches.
2391.nuance: தானம் may be 'place' or 'gift'. சந்நிதி சேட்டிப்ப (the presence acting) and தோயா (untouched, not soaked) are taken in the Siddhanta sense that the Lord acts through his powers by mere presence and is not stained by the acts. The verse is compressed.

2392.reading: They say the 'thou' of Vedanta is the bound soul; the good Lord is what stands when the bond at the end of nada is let go, the 'that' of bodhanta; going on, the union of the two, held in common, is Siva-sayujya.
2392.nuance: The verse maps tat tvam asi onto the Siddhanta categories: 'thou' is pasu, 'that' is pati, 'art' is sayujya. சாதாரணம் (common) is unclear: perhaps the union shared by both schools, or the state common to soul and Lord.

2393.reading: Becoming Siva is Vedanta and Siddhanta; apart from that, each of the two is in vain; if Sadasiva, who is Siva, made them one, the new Vedanta is the Siddhanta of knowledge.
2393.nuance: அவம் அவம் ஆகும் அவ்வவ் இரண்டும் may mean either is futile unless it leads to becoming Siva, or that the two taken apart are futile. நவமான may be 'new' or 'ninefold'.

2394.reading: Since in Siddhanta the soul attains release while living, those who stand in Siddhanta attain release and siddhi; since Siddhanta and Vedanta are the perfect meaning, Siddhanta and Vedanta show Siva.
2394.nuance: Lines 1 and 2 (சித்தித்திலால், சித்தித்திவர்) are a play on சித்தி whose exact form is unclear; சீவன் முத்தி is release while living. செம்பொருள் (the perfect meaning) is the Kural's word in 358.

2395.reading: If Vedanta and Siddhanta, free of waste, show Siva within the Supreme and within the soul, then knowledge, made new in the states, becomes Siva; those who have realised this, rich in austerity, are the people of truth.
2395.nuance: அவத்தை are the states of the soul (waking, dream and the rest), a Siddhanta term. நவமுற்று may be 'made new' or 'reaching the ninth'. தத்துவத்தார் plays forward into 2396, which opens with தத்துவம்.

2396.reading: Tattva is the formed and the formless; tattva is bindu, nada and Sadasiva; tattva is the soul and its Supreme; tattva is Siva-sayujya.
2396.nuance: தத்துவம் opens every line. It can be the tattvas as constituents of the world, which fits bindu and nada, or 'truth, reality', which fits the soul, the Supreme and sayujya; the verse seems to use both. சகளம், அகளம் are the Lord with parts and without.

2397.reading: The Veda and the Agama are the scriptures of the true Lord; what they teach is called the general and the special; examined, both are the Lord's word; people call the two ends different, but for the great they are not different.
2397.nuance: The Veda as பொது (general, for all) and the Agama as சிறப்பு (special, for the qualified) is a well-known Saiva position, and this verse is often cited for it. The 'two ends' are taken as Vedanta and Siddhanta.

2398.reading: All the bliss of Siva in which Paranandi abides: the supreme bliss, the three above, the bliss that never goes to waste, the bliss of the seal of rest, the bliss of the true dance; the heart that stands without strife swells with them.
2398.nuance: The verse lists kinds of bliss whose number and order are unclear; விராமுத்திரானந்தம் is read as the bliss of the mudra of cessation (விராம). பொராநின்ற உள்ளம் may be 'the heart that does not contend' or 'the heart that strives'.

2399.reading: Kalanta, the two ends and nadanta: when they come about, the kalas are five; so Hara is the Lord of the five ends, as he said in the Veda and the Agama.
2399.nuance: Here the ends are counted as five (பஞ்சாந்தம்), not six; 2400 suggests why, taking Vedanta and Siddhanta as one. இரண்டந்தம் (the two ends) may be those two, as in 2397.

2400.reading: Not rejecting the five kinds of end, and holding them together with Vedanta and Siddhanta made one, yoganta comes right; when it comes right, one reaches the feet of the dancer in the hall.
2400.nuance: அன்றாகும் என்னாது is read as 'without saying it is not so'. அன்னை (mother) after ஐவகை அந்தம் is unclear: the Shakti, or a misreading. மன்றாடி is the dancer in the hall at Chidambaram.

2401.reading: The beginningless soul, free of the five malas and gone beyond, restraining what is beginningless, sees itself, becomes Hara, its own primal malam destroyed, beyond the tattvas, as water becomes milk: this is the truth of Vedanta.
2401.nuance: ஐம்மலம் is traditionally the five bonds (anava, karma, maya, mayeya, tirodhana). Water mixed into milk is a classic image of union in which the two can no longer be told apart. That the verse calls this Vedanta's truth matches the chapter's claim that Vedanta and Siddhanta agree. வினாவு (asking) in line 4 is unclear and may be a misprint for விரவு (mixing).

2402.reading: Knowing without weariness the soul and the Supreme, the soul and Siva, is 'thou art that'; so, action ceasing, becoming knowledge and going to subside there, is the unwearying Vedanta and Siddhanta.
2402.nuance: தொந்தத்தசி is tvam tat asi, the great saying with its words in this order. Line 3 gives the sequence: action ends, the soul becomes knowledge, then subsides in Siva.

2403.reading: The abiding 'So'ham' is the crowning Siva-yoga of those who know the great Veda; and that same thing, as the meaning of the great scripture of Siddhanta, appears as the Agama joined with it.
2403.nuance: சோகம் (so'ham, 'I am He') is a meditation formula. The verse makes one teaching appear as Siva-yoga for Veda-knowers and as Agama for Siddhantins; the syntax of lines 3 and 4 is loose.

2404.reading: The Veda that comes first and the whole Agama are the two that Isa, the Lord within, spoke; the ancient Veda, set in its due order, they become the foremost Vedanta and Siddhanta.
2404.nuance: அகப் பதி may be the Lord within, or பதி alone as the Siddhanta Lord. அதிகாதி in line 4 is unclear: perhaps 'foremost' or அதிகாரி (one qualified).

links.note: 1449 mentions the six of wide Vedanta and Siddhanta without listing them, if மாறும் is read as ஆறும்; 2370 names the six ends, Vedanta and Siddhanta first.
2381 turns the ends into the triad of knowing, known and knower; 2382 then dissolves the triad itself, ends into known, knower into known, knowledge gone, leaving silence and bliss.
Both make silence a mudra, a seal: 1900 calls the seal of silence the mark of the liberated, and 2386 ends the unity of Vedanta and Siddhanta in sinking into the silence of the seal.

1509 ends the grades of release when the bond dissolves and the Lord is sayujya; 2392 reads tat tvam asi onto the same scheme: 'thou' is the soul, 'that' the Lord left when the bond goes, and their union sayujya.
1435 calls Siddhanta not other than Vedanta; 2393 says both are the one aim of becoming Siva, each in vain apart from it.
2399 counts the ends as five, not six; 2400 holds the five together with Vedanta and Siddhanta made one, which explains the count.
Both make the Veda and the Agama the Lord's own speech and, read rightly, the source of one Vedanta-Siddhanta; 2397 adds that the Veda is general and the Agama special.
2017 says soul and Siva are not different and that souls who know Siva remain as Siva; 2402 calls that knowing of soul and Siva the meaning of tat tvam asi.
Both call what true knowledge reaches செம்பொருள், the perfect thing, and tie it to release. The Kural leaves it unnamed; Tirumular says Siddhanta and Vedanta are that perfect meaning and show Siva.

2372 joins Vedanta, which has become the self, and Siddhanta, which declares it, in Siva-yoga that removes malam and gives the rare attainment (அரும்சித்தி). 1428 places the knower's dawning knowledge and true release in the joined portion of Vedanta and Siddhanta (வேதாந்த சித்தாந்த பாகத்தின் ஊடுறு ஞானோதயன்). Both make release lie where the two ends meet.

2373 makes Siddhanta the soul's reaching the Father, holding that neither pure nor impure follows it (சுத்தம் அசுத்தம் தொடரா வகை). 1420 says the pure Saivas stand untouched by pure and impure (சுத்தம் அசுத்தமும் தோய்வுறாமே நின்று) and hold the Supreme dear. The same phrase defines Siddhanta in one and the pure Saiva in the other.

2374 says that when the thirty-six cease, the soul alone remains (ஓவும் பொழுதுஅணு ஒன்றுஉளதாம்). 2197 traces the same falling away of tattvas through waking into deep sleep and finds there 'maya alone' (இதில்மாயை தானே). Shedding the tattvas leaves the soul alone only at nadanta; in sleep the same shedding leaves maya.

2380 ends kalanta in Nandi, beyond speech, word and feeling (பேசா உரையுணர்வற்ற), beyond speech and mind (வாசாமகோசரம்). 2854 bids the reader look at the hidden thing where speech and mind disappear (வாக்கும் மனமும் மறைந்த மறைபொருள்). The same limit marks the goal in both, and 2854 adds that it can still be looked at.

2387 and 2392 are near-repeats reading tat tvam asi: 'thou' (தொம்பதம்) is the soul freed at nadanta, 'that' (தற்பதம்) is the Supreme at bodhanta. 2392 names them pasu and pati and calls the 'art' Siva-sayujya, where 2387 counts seven adjuncts on each side; the repeat fixes the Saiva reading of the saying.

2388 places within the great light beyond the seven worlds an inner light called Parashakti, and the Lord stands there holding her, yet not as her. 1768 puts Parashakti above Shakti and within her the pure state of Siva, an untouched light (தோயாத தூவொளி). Both set Siva within Parashakti and yet distinct from her.

2390 says that though souls do not think of the One, of themselves, their two deeds or the two mayas, the One stands within and feeds them (உள் உணர்ந்து நின்று ஊட்டி). The Kural says that even those who amass millions can enjoy only as the apportioner apportioned (வகுத்தான் வகுத்த வகையல்லால்). 2390 names who the apportioner is and makes the feeding inward.

2390 has the One stand within and feed the souls (ஒருவனுமேயுள் உணர்ந்துநின் றூட்டி). 2421 says the Lord kindly feeds the soul its experience through the maya he set working (மாயையில் ஊட்டல் பரிந்தனன்). 2421 shows the feeding as grace that leads toward his feet, not only as fate.

2391 calls Hara the steady one of Siva's bliss whom nothing touches (தோயாச் சிவாநந்தி), though he acts through his powers. 1538 says pure Siva stands everywhere untouched (தோய்வற்று நிற்கின்றான்). Both use தோய் for the Lord who pervades and acts yet is not stained.

2206 reads the states as stages of knowing that end in knowledge become knowledge as turiya (அறிவுஅறிவாகும் ஆன துரியமே). 2395 says that when Vedanta and Siddhanta show Siva within, knowledge made new in the states becomes Siva (அவத்தையில் ஞானம் சிவமாம்). 2395 names the goal the states of 2206 lead to.

2398 lists the kinds of Siva's bliss, among them the bliss of the true dance (மெய்நடன ஆனந்தம்), which fill the heart that does not contend. 2635 has Nandi dance in the great bliss beyond speech (பேச்சற்ற பேரின்பத்து அம்மா நடிதந்து) and asks the soul to stay still. Both make the dance the form the bliss takes.

2401 ends with the soul become Hara as water becomes milk (நீர் பாலாதல்). Naladiyar 177 says water mixed with milk becomes milk and no longer shows its own colour (பாலோடு அளாயநீர் பாலாகும்), of small men joined to the great. The same image of losing one's colour in a greater body is used of company in the Naladiyar and of the soul's union with Siva in 2401.

source_issues: 2375 line 3 reads ஓர்iஉணர் with a stray Latin letter; read ஓர் உணர்வு.
2384 line 4 கூளி gives no fitting sense; perhaps கூறி.
2401 line 4 வினாவுநீர் may be a misprint for விரவுநீர் (mixed water).
2383: the numbers of kalas and ends (six in five, two with five making seven) do not resolve into a clear scheme; the verse may be corrupt.
2378: mantra, tantra, upadesa and jnana make four, though the verse says five.
2394 lines 1 and 2 (சித்தித்திலால், சித்தித்திவர்) and 2404 line 4 (அதிகாதி) are obscure and may be corrupt.
